summary: A torsion-sensitive delta/Frobenius/Witt foundation, extended by the precise ordinary-localization criterion: a compatible delta structure exists uniquely exactly when the images of Frobenius denominators are units. The construction uses the actual length-two Witt ring and existing localization universal property, without cancelling p or replacing the ring by a torsionfree quotient. All sixteen preceding nodes are preserved; twelve nodes add the coefficient adapter, unit criterion, two API promotions, localization construction, uniqueness, universal property, fraction formula and the source Frobenius-stable specialization. Prism and cohomology work remains explicit and partial.

nodes.title: Integral addition correction
nodes.statement: Define C_p(x,y) as minus the sum over 1<=i<=p-1 of (binomial(p,i)/p) x^i y^(p-i). The quotient is an exact natural/integer coefficient, then cast to R. Never divide by p in R.
hypotheses: p is prime; R is a commutative unital ring, possibly zero or with p-torsion.
proofSteps: Use the pinned prime-binomial divisibility theorem to justify each integral coefficient.
Evaluate this fixed integer polynomial in the existing ring. Finite sums, powers and the index involution i->p-i give the API.
acceptance: C_2=-xy and C_3=-xy(x+y).
The formula evaluates when p is zero or a zero divisor in R.

sources.match: Makes the integral polynomial underlying the displayed addition axiom explicit.

uses.where: PR.0 delta axioms and Witt-coordinate comparison
uses.how: Pins the sign and retains the addition law in p-torsion rings.

nodes.title: Cleared-denominator correction identity
nodes.statement: In every commutative ring, p C_p(x,y)=x^p+y^p-(x+y)^p.
hypotheses: p is prime. Multiplication by p need not be injective in R.
proofSteps: Multiply the finite sum by p and use exact integer divisibility of its coefficients.
Apply the pinned binomial theorem and separate its i=0 and i=p terms. No cancellation in R is used.
acceptance: The identity holds in characteristic p, although it cannot recover C_p there.

sources.match: Explicit polynomial justification of the correction, not division in the target.

nodes.title: Delta structure on a ring
nodes.statement: On the existing ring R, a delta structure is a function delta:R->R with delta(0)=delta(1)=0, delta(x+y)=delta(x)+delta(y)+C_p(x,y), and delta(xy)=x^p delta(y)+y^p delta(x)+p delta(x)delta(y). Morphisms are unital ring maps commuting with delta. Retain the integrated dictionary ID for this definition; its two equivalences are separate construction nodes.
hypotheses: p is prime; R is a commutative unital ring.
The elementary polynomial prefix is generalized to rings; subsequent prismatic consumers retain the source Z_(p)-algebra hypotheses.
proofSteps: Package precisely the four polynomial axioms as data on R, not an assumed comparison theorem. Delta is not an additive map.
Prove extensionality from equality of the functions. Apply the addition law to x+(-x) and to 1+1 for the elementary API.
acceptance: The zero operation on Z is not a delta structure.
A delta structure alone is not a prism: no ideal or completion is supplied.

sources.match: Preserves the actual axioms and distinguishes the elementary generalization from the source's prismatic scope.

uses.how: The product identity controls delta of a product.
Import one-prime delta data, not a second construction or all-prime commuting lifts.

nodes.title: Ordinary Frobenius lift
nodes.statement: A FrobeniusLift is a unital endomorphism f of R such that for each x there exists y with f(x)=x^p+p y. Equivalently its reduction modulo (p) is Frobenius. The witnesses form a proposition, not a chosen delta operation or a derived homotopy.
hypotheses: p is prime; R is a commutative unital ring.
proofSteps: Use the subtype of the existing RingHom R R cut out by the pointwise divisibility property.
The kernel description of the quotient by (p) gives the quotient characterization. Equality of lifts is equality of their ring maps.
acceptance: The identity on F_p is a lift although F_p has no delta structure.
A map of sets such as x->x^p on Z is not substituted for a ring map.

sources.match: Names the ordinary congruence datum and explicitly does not replace the derived datum.

uses.how: Records exactly the ordinary data from which cancellation can recover a unique delta.

nodes.title: Associated Frobenius endomorphism
nodes.statement: Construct the ordinary lift phi_delta(x)=x^p+p delta(x) from a delta structure, for arbitrary commutative rings including p-torsion.
hypotheses: p is prime; use the given delta structure on R.
proofSteps: Zero and unit follow from the corresponding delta axioms.
For addition expand the delta law and use correction-identity. For multiplication expand the delta product law and factor as phi(x)phi(y).
Delta(x) supplies the congruence witness. A delta-compatible ring map commutes with phi by the same expansion.
acceptance: No converse without a cancellation hypothesis is asserted.

sources.match: Builds the ring-map laws rather than assuming the associated endomorphism.

nodes.title: Torsion-free Frobenius reconstruction
nodes.statement: If multiplication by p on R is injective, construct an equivalence between delta structures and ordinary Frobenius lifts, with forward map associated-frobenius. CharZero alone is not sufficient.
hypotheses: p is prime. Multiplication by the cast of p on R is injective; the zero ring is permitted.
proofSteps: The congruence gives a solution delta(x) of p delta(x)=f(x)-x^p, unique by injectivity. Choose it pointwise.

Multiply each proposed delta axiom by p. Addition uses correction-identity; multiplication expands (x^p+p delta(x))(y^p+p delta(y)). The differences are the additivity and multiplicativity errors of f, hence zero. Cancel only the remaining factor p.
Both composites are identities by the same uniqueness and ring-map extensionality. The public equivalence does not depend on witness choices.
acceptance: The zero ring meets the injectivity condition vacuously.
A characteristic-zero ring with a p-torsion ideal need not meet it.

sources.match: Retains exactly the p-torsionfree reconstruction hypothesis and constructs both inverses.

uses.how: Converts a constructed lift into delta only after checking p-torsionfreeness.

nodes.title: Frobenius compatibility detects delta morphisms
nodes.statement: For delta rings R,S and a ring map f:R->S, if multiplication by p is injective on S, then f commutes with delta exactly when it commutes with associated Frobenius. No cancellation hypothesis on R is needed.
hypotheses: p is prime; f is unital; target multiplication by p is injective.
proofSteps: Delta compatibility implies Frobenius compatibility by expansion.
For the converse expand Frobenius compatibility, cancel the common f(x)^p terms, and cancel multiplication by p in S.
acceptance: Without target cancellation the identity map between the two square-zero structures is a counterexample.

sources.match: The explicit morphism form, with cancellation only in the target.

nodes.title: Canonical delta operation on the integers
nodes.statement: Construct the canonical delta structure on Z with D_p(a)=(a-a^p)/p, using exact integer division. Its associated Frobenius is the identity. This is the integral elementary prefix of the source p-local example.
hypotheses: p is prime. Negative integers and p=2 are included.
proofSteps: Apply FiniteField.pow_card in F_p to show that p divides a-a^p for every integer a.
The identity map on Z is an ordinary lift. Multiplication by the nonzero integer p is injective, so apply the established reconstruction.
The inverse equation gives the quotient formula and, at a=p, D_p(p)=1-p^(p-1).
acceptance: D_2(-1)=-1, whereas at odd p it is zero.

sources.match: Restricts the source formula to Z and proves its integrality; it does not identify Z with Z_(p).

uses.how: Pins scalar, negative-integer and dyadic conventions.

nodes.title: Delta on integer scalars
nodes.statement: For every delta structure on R and integer a, delta(a*1_R) is the cast of the integer (a-a^p)/p. Consequently a nonzero ring of characteristic p has no delta structure.
hypotheses: p is prime. Do not assume p-torsionfreeness of R.
proofSteps: In Z, verify D(n+1)=D(n)+C_p(n,1) by multiplying by p and cancelling in Z.

The addition axiom gives the same recurrence after casting to R. Start at zero, induct upwards for nonnegative integers and run the recurrence backwards for negative integers. Only additive cancellation is used in R.
Evaluate at a=p: if p=0 in R then 0=delta(0)=1-p^(p-1)=1 because p>=2.
acceptance: This does not rule out some p-torsion in a mixed-characteristic ring.
Retain the dyadic negative-scalar value.

sources.match: Direct scalar proof for arbitrary targets, without assuming initiality of an unconstructed category.

nodes.title: Descent to a delta-stable quotient
nodes.statement: For a delta structure on R and an ideal I, delta(I) contained in I is equivalent to existence of a unique delta structure on R/I compatible with the quotient map.
hypotheses: p is prime; use the actual ideal and quotient ring.
proofSteps: Replacing a representative a by a+i changes delta(a) by delta(i)+C_p(a,i). Stability puts the first term in I; every monomial of the correction has a positive power of i, so the second lies in I.
Descend the four polynomial axioms. Surjectivity of the quotient gives uniqueness. Conversely, compatibility on an element of I puts its delta in the kernel.
acceptance: I=0 returns the original operation and I=R gives the zero ring.
The ideal (p) in canonical Z is Frobenius-stable but not delta-stable, since delta(p)=1-p^(p-1).

sources.match: The quotient construction with its necessary stability and uniqueness conditions.

nodes.title: Correction polynomial on a square-zero extension
nodes.statement: Let B map to F_p and use its central action. In the existing square-zero extension B plus F_p, the second coordinate of C_p((a,b),(c,d)) is (abar^(p-1)-(abar+cbar)^(p-1))*b+(cbar^(p-1)-(abar+cbar)^(p-1))*d.
hypotheses: p is prime; B is commutative; the left action comes from the unital B->F_p map and the opposite action is central.
proofSteps: Expand powers with snd_pow and products with snd_mul. Termwise, a finite polynomial has second coordinate its first partial derivative times b plus its second partial derivative times d.
Differentiate the integral polynomial identity p C_p(X,Y)=X^p+Y^p-(X+Y)^p termwise, then cancel p in Z[X,Y]. This gives partial_X C_p=X^(p-1)-(X+Y)^(p-1) and the Y analogue.
Evaluate these already-integral identities in F_p. No division or cancellation occurs there.
acceptance: At p=2 the result is -cbar*b-abar*d, the second coordinate of -xy.

sources.match: An explicit polynomial deduction, not a separately numbered source lemma.
The existing square-zero coordinate arithmetic.

nodes.title: Delta structures on a square-zero extension
nodes.statement: For a delta ring B mapping to F_p and lambda in F_p, define delta_lambda(a,b)=(delta_B(a),(lambda-abar^(p-1))*b) on the existing central square-zero extension B plus F_p. This is a delta structure with associated Frobenius (a,b)->(phi_B(a),0).
hypotheses: p is prime. The left scalar action on F_p is induced by the displayed ring map and the opposite action is central.
proofSteps: The first coordinates of the four axioms are those for B; zero and unit in the second coordinate are immediate.
For addition insert square-zero-correction. The second coordinate simplifies to (lambda-(abar+cbar)^(p-1))*(b+d).
For multiplication the second coordinates of x^p and y^p vanish, and so does that of p delta(x)delta(y). Use abar^p=abar and cbar^p=cbar to get (lambda-(abar*cbar)^(p-1))*(abar*d+cbar*b).
The power formula also gives the stated associated Frobenius, independent of lambda.
acceptance: The proof works at p=2.
B=Z supplies integer tests; B=Z_(p) with its canonical delta supplies a source-compatible p-local example.

sources.match: An explicit acceptance family explaining the cancellation hypothesis, not a source erratum.
The ring already exists; only its delta operation is constructed here.

uses.how: Detects loss of delta information on p-torsion, including over a characteristic-zero base.

api.name: TauCeti.Delta.squareZeroDelta_frobenius
api.statement: Frobenius is inl(phi_B(a)), independent of lambda.

tests.name: square_zero_parameter
tests.statement: For B=Z and epsilon=(0,1), delta_lambda(epsilon)=lambda*epsilon.

tests.name: square_zero_base_compatibility

nodes.title: Distinct delta structures with the same Frobenius
nodes.statement: For lambda different from mu in F_p, the square-zero structures on B plus F_p differ but have the same associated lift. With B=Z the ring has characteristic zero; with B=Z_(p) it is p-local. Ordinary Frobenius data need not determine delta.
hypotheses: The base and scalar actions are those of square-zero-delta-family; lambda and mu are distinct.
proofSteps: At epsilon=(0,1) the values are inr(lambda) and inr(mu), distinct by injectivity of inr.
Both associated maps send (a,b) to inl(phi_B(a)); ring-map extensionality proves equality.

For the p-local example, (a-a^p)/p lies in Z_(p) by reduction to F_p, and multiplication by p is injective. Reconstruct its canonical base structure, then apply the general family. The integer ring is not silently treated as p-local.
acceptance: The identity between the two structures is Frobenius-compatible but not delta-compatible.
For lambda=1, phi(epsilon)=epsilon^p=0 while delta(epsilon)=epsilon is nonzero, rejecting the rank-one converse.

sources.match: A concrete failure of strengthened hypotheses, not an allegation of an error in the source.

nodes.title: Second coordinate of length-two Witt addition
nodes.statement: On TruncatedWittVector p 2 R, (x+y)_1=x_1+y_1+C_p(x_0,y_0), for arbitrary commutative R.
hypotheses: p is prime; use the existing Witt ring operations, not pointwise operations.
proofSteps: First work over the integer polynomial ring in four input coordinates. Use ghost components 0 and 1 as ring maps and the first two Witt polynomials. Subtract the zeroth-coordinate pth powers and cancel p only in this universal ring. correction-identity identifies the correction.

Evaluate the variables in R using WittVector.map and map_coeff, then truncate the infinite universal vectors. Surjectivity and unchanged coordinates give the formula for every truncated vector. Zero-padding is only a lift of sets, not a ring map.
acceptance: Over F_2, (1,0)+(1,0)=(0,1), rejecting pointwise addition.

sources.match: Constructs the coordinate formula on the existing carrier by universal polynomial descent, not ghost injectivity in R.

nodes.title: Second coordinate of length-two Witt multiplication
nodes.statement: On TruncatedWittVector p 2 R, (xy)_1=x_0^p*y_1+y_0^p*x_1+p*x_1*y_1.
hypotheses: p is prime; R is arbitrary commutative and unital.
proofSteps: In the universal integer polynomial ring expand (x_0^p+p*x_1)(y_0^p+p*y_1), subtract (x_0*y_0)^p, and cancel p there.
Transport using coefficientwise Witt maps and truncation to R. The zeroth product coordinate follows from constantCoeff as a ring map. No cancellation in R is used.
acceptance: Keep p*x_1*y_1 before specializing to characteristic p.

sources.match: The multiplication coordinate calculation is its own declaration.

nodes.title: Delta structures as Witt-vector sections
nodes.statement: For arbitrary R, construct an equivalence between delta structures and unital ring maps s:R->TruncatedWittVector p 2 R whose first coordinate is s(x)_0=x. Send delta to s(x)=(x,delta(x)); recover delta from coordinate one. This is a first-coordinate section, not a ghost-map section.
hypotheses: p is prime; no p-torsionfreeness hypothesis on R.
proofSteps: Given delta, construct the two-coordinate vector. The two preceding Witt formulas and delta axioms give preservation of addition and multiplication. Zero and one have coordinates (0,0) and (1,0).
Given a ring-map section, take its second coordinate. The ring-map laws and coordinate formulas give all four delta axioms.

Coefficient extensionality and the first-coordinate condition prove both inverse identities. The first ghost expression x^p+p delta(x) identifies the composite with associated Frobenius, without cancellation in R.
acceptance: Distinct square-zero delta structures give distinct Witt sections despite identical associated Frobenius.

sources.locator: Remark 2.4, pp.13-14; section condition visually read on p.14
sources.match: The source dictionary with an explicit bridge to the pinned truncated Witt ring.

uses.where: PR.0 free delta-algebra, localization and Witt-adjunction work
uses.how: Supplies torsion-safe underived data before the full adjunction or derived comparison is constructed.

nodes.title: Naturality of the integral correction
nodes.statement: For a unital ring map f:R->T, f(C_p(x,y))=C_p(f(x),f(y)). This promotes the existing addCorrection_map API without introducing a second declaration.
hypotheses: p is prime; R and T are commutative rings, including rings with p-torsion.
proofSteps: Apply the ring map to the finite sum defining C_p. Each integer coefficient, power and product is preserved. The division was performed in the integers before evaluation.
acceptance: Reduction to characteristic p retains the correction polynomial.

sources.locator: Definition 2.1: integral addition polynomial; existing addCorrection_map API

nodes.title: Coefficient map on length-two Witt vectors
nodes.statement: For a ring map f:R->T construct witt2Map(f):W_2(R)->W_2(T) with both Witt coordinates mapped by f, using the existing TruncatedWittVector p 2 carrier.
hypotheses: p is prime; R,T are commutative rings. No torsion-freeness or condition on the Jacobson radical.
proofSteps: Apply f coordinatewise. The zeroth-coordinate, zero and unit rules follow from the pinned infinite Witt map and surjective coordinate-preserving truncation.

The second addition-coordinate formula and correction-map-naturality give additivity. The second multiplication-coordinate formula gives multiplicativity by applying f to each factor and integer coefficient. Package the resulting map as a RingHom.
Prove identity and composition by equality of both coordinates. This is a length-two adapter; it does not rebuild truncated Witt rings.

nodes.title: Units in length-two Witt vectors
nodes.statement: For z=(a,b) in W_2(R), z is a unit if and only if both a and a^p+p*b are units of R.
hypotheses: p is prime; R is an arbitrary commutative ring, possibly zero.
proofSteps: An inverse z*(c,d)=1 gives ac=1. Expanding the first ghost polynomial of the product gives (a^p+p*b)(c^p+p*d)=1. Hence both factors specified in the statement are units.

Conversely, put g=a^p+p*b and use the actual inverses of the units a and g. The Witt vector (a^(-1),-b*a^(-p)*g^(-1)) has product with z equal to (1,0): its second coordinate is g*(-b*a^(-p)*g^(-1))+a^(-p)*b=0. Commutativity gives a two-sided inverse.
Zeroth-coordinate and one-coordinate rules are obtained from constantCoeff and surjective truncation. No p-cancellation or ghost injectivity over R is used.
acceptance: For p=2 over Z, (1,1) is not a unit although its first coordinate is.
Over F_p the criterion reduces to invertibility of a.
The unique vector over the zero ring is a unit.

nodes.title: Coordinates of the delta Witt section

proofSteps: Use the defined forward map of the Witt-section equivalence and coefficient extensionality. Its inverse identities also recover these coordinates for a section from which the delta structure was reconstructed.

nodes.title: Localization of a delta structure
nodes.statement: Let B be an A-algebra carrying IsLocalization S B and let i:A->B be its algebra map. Given a delta structure on A and units i(phi(s)) for every s in S, construct a delta structure localize on B compatible with i. No injectivity of i or multiplication by p is required.
hypotheses: p is prime; A,B are commutative rings; S is a submonoid of A.
The image-unit condition is in B; it is not an assertion that phi(S) is literally contained in S.
proofSteps: Compose the actual Witt section A->W_2(A) with witt2Map(i). It sends a to (i(a),i(delta(a))). For s in S its first coordinate is a unit by localization and its first ghost expression is i(phi(s)), a unit by hypothesis. The Witt unit criterion makes this section image a unit.
Apply the existing ring IsLocalization.lift to obtain a map s_B:B->W_2(B). The first-coordinate projection is a ring map, as verified using constantCoeff and surjective truncation.
The composite of that projection with s_B agrees with id_B on i(A), by lift_eq. Localization ringHom_ext proves equality on B, so s_B is a first-coordinate section.
Apply the existing inverse Witt-section equivalence to s_B. Its inverse identities and the coefficient formula give the resulting operation on B. Fraction representatives are not used to define it.
acceptance: The result is a delta structure on the given B, not a new localization ring or a p-torsionfree quotient.

nodes.title: Uniqueness of localized delta data
nodes.statement: Under the localization construction hypotheses, every delta structure e on B compatible with i:A->B equals localize. In particular the construction is independent of proofs of the image-unit condition.
hypotheses: B carries the actual IsLocalization S B instance.
Compatibility means equality of delta operations on the image of A, not merely compatibility of Frobenius.
proofSteps: Take the Witt sections of e and localize. Their first coordinates on i(a) coincide, and their second coordinates coincide by compatibility and localized-delta-on-base.

Truncated Witt extensionality gives equality of the two sections after precomposition with i. Localization ringHom_ext gives equality on all B; injectivity of the Witt-section equivalence gives equality of structures.
acceptance: Coincidence of associated Frobenius alone is not used; it would be insufficient on p-torsion.

nodes.title: Criterion for extension across a localization
nodes.statement: A delta structure on A extends compatibly to B=S^(-1)A if and only if each i(phi(s)) is a unit in B. When it extends it is unique. Equivalently each phi(s) divides some element of S.
hypotheses: p is prime; A and B are commutative rings; IsLocalization S B specifies i.
proofSteps: Sufficiency is delta-localization and localized-delta-on-base; uniqueness is delta-localization-unique.
For necessity, a compatible extension has associated ring endomorphism phi_B. Expanding x^p+p*delta(x) gives phi_B(i(s))=i(phi_A(s)). Ring homomorphisms carry the unit i(s) to a unit.
The pinned algebraMap_isUnit_iff expresses the image-unit condition as the stated divisibility/saturation condition. It needs no domain hypothesis.
acceptance: In A=Z_(p)[X] with phi(X)=X^p+p, the localization A[X^-1] has no compatible delta structure: X^p+p is not a Laurent unit.
For p=2 on Z plus F_2*epsilon and s=(3,1), phi(s)=(3,0) divides s^2 but is not a power of s. Literal stability is not necessary.

nodes.title: Universal property in delta rings
nodes.statement: Let e be any compatible extension of d from A to the localization B. For a delta-compatible ring map f:A->C sending S to units, there is a unique ring map g:B->C extending f and commuting with delta. Its underlying map is the existing IsLocalization.lift.
hypotheses: p is prime; C is a commutative ring with a specified delta structure; no p-torsionfreeness of C.
proofSteps: Take g to be the existing ring localization lift; lift_eq gives its base values.

Compare the maps witt2Map(g) composed with the Witt section of e, and the Witt section of C composed with g. On i(a), their two coordinates agree by the compatibility of e and f and the base values of g.

Use truncated Witt extensionality and localization ringHom_ext. Equality of second coordinates gives delta compatibility on all B. Any other candidate agrees with g on i(A), hence equals it as a ring map.
acceptance: Identity and composite maps are compatible by the unique extension property.
This proof works even when different delta structures can have the same Frobenius.

nodes.title: Delta of a fraction
nodes.statement: For z=mk'(B,a,s), the constructed delta satisfies i(s)^p*i(phi(s))*delta_B(z)=i(s)^p*i(delta(a))-i(a)^p*i(delta(s)). The coefficient of delta_B(z) is a unit, so this determines the value without dividing by p.
hypotheses: The data and unit condition are those of delta-localization; a is in A and s is in S.
proofSteps: The existing mk'_spec' gives i(s)*z=i(a). Apply the product axiom and localized-delta-on-base to obtain i(delta(a))=i(phi(s))*delta_B(z)+z^p*i(delta(s)).
Multiply by i(s)^p and use (i(s)*z)^p=i(a)^p. The image-unit condition and map_units show the coefficient is a unit. This calculation also proves independence of the chosen expression for z.
acceptance: For the canonical integer structure at p=2, delta(1/3)=1/9.
For phi(X)=X^p+p in the rational function field, delta(X^-1)=-1/(X^p*(X^p+p)); replacing the second denominator by X^p is false.

nodes.title: Frobenius-stable localizations
nodes.statement: If phi(S) is contained in S, the given delta structure on A extends uniquely to its ordinary localization at S, and the extension has the delta-morphism universal property.
hypotheses: p is prime. The elementary ring statement holds generally; the source instance retains A as a Z_(p)-algebra.
proofSteps: For each s in S, its Frobenius image is another denominator, hence has unit image by map_units.

Apply delta-localization-criterion for existence and uniqueness and delta-localization-universal for the morphism property. No free delta algebra, completion or assumption of p-torsionfreeness is imported into this alternative proof.
